tr.td: phase ≥ 3 and t − transition_start ≥ reelout_delay and !reelout_done

v_set from the kv·√force law (through the ramps on the left); l_set integrates it, clamped at reelout_l_max; rc is stepped (on_timer). v_set is passed to step! twice over: integrated into l_set and fed forward as v_ff, which removes the 1/winch_pos_kp = 2 s lag the integrate-here / differentiate-there pair would otherwise have. reelout_done latches once either l_set ≥ reelout_l_max or n_fig_eight laps have flown, whichever comes first.

guard_lfc, a standalone LowerForceController, reels in (its output is clamped to ≤ 0) if the measured force sags below rcs.f_low — only while guard_lfc.active. Otherwise v_set = 0 and l_set stays flat.
neither — i.e. phase 3/4 before reelout_delay has elapsed, or phase 5

div.b: Why the guard is not rc
div.font:
Stepping the full WinchController through the entry lets its SpeedController integrator wind up while its output is ignored, which dumps a saturated +v_sat command the moment it is first used (measured). A bare LowerForceController has no such integrator, and rc's soft-start clock stays at 0 until phase 3.
Note the asymmetry: the guard runs in phases 0–2 only. In the window between phase 3 and reelout_delay expiring there is no force floor, on the assumption that the guidance is already loading the wing by then.

div.div:
The two ramps — both default to 0 in FC_Settings, which disables them
Soft-start: ramp = clamp((t − transition_start − reelout_delay) / reelout_softstart, 0, 1) scales the command only — rc's internal integrators and force limiters still see the unscaled v_raw, so it shapes the engagement transient without lagging the steady-state force regulation.
Soft-stop: latches once, when EITHER remaining ≤ v_cmd · reelout_softstop (the length criterion) OR fig8_idx_progress ≥ n_fig_eight · n_path (the lap criterion), with v_cmd > 0 and reelout_softstop > 0. For the length criterion, stop_start = t, stop_v_entry = v_cmd and stop_T = 2 · remaining / v_cmd — a linear ramp's area is v_entry · T / 2, so the time is solved exactly, not guessed (it comes out at roughly 2 × reelout_softstop), and v_set reaches 0 exactly at reelout_l_max. The lap criterion has no remaining distance to solve from, so it latches stop_T = 2 · reelout_softstop directly — the same nominal duration — and lands wherever that puts l_set. Either way v_set = stop_v_entry · (1 − clamp((t − stop_start)/stop_T, 0, 1)) and reelout_done latches true once the ramp runs out (or immediately, as a hard stop, if reelout_softstop = 0). The latch is never cleared, so soft-stop is terminal within the reel-out branch. stop_reason records which criterion fired first.
